reviews.text: Bullshit. You can't make a film about how women are exploited in media while having a crew of almost all men. This is a film about how women suffer, but it's made by men and for men. There were so unnecessary scenes that were clearly just for the male gaze. No one can change my mind about this one sorry.

I understand what this movie was attempting to do, but I don’t think any amount of visual intrigue is enough to make up for the voyeuristic way in which the violence it claims to be criticizing is portrayed. Not only that, but the critiques are surface level at best. The plot twist was cheap and did very little to advance the story in a way that actually said anything. I have no problem watching a film that is uncomfortable as long as it has substance, but this film just left me sick to my stomach with nothing to chew on.

one of the most overrated "masterpieces" out there. any level of graphic abuse gets played out at length for aesthetic effect dressed up as "important for the plot." the heaviness of that abuse is downplayed and is used just as a tool to keep the thriller moving.This didn’t feel like a wake up call on the dark side of the industry, it felt like it was part of it. 1/2 star for good colour grading

AHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH I really dislike this genre of violent SA in pop-movies (which that is not to say this is at all a pop-film, but the current trend of films like Obsession that leave a very sour feeling in my mouth) and it makes me very triggered every time. It really stands in the way of this film being enjoyable at all. While the themes extend insightful ideation on identity, hetero-patriarchy, sex-desire capitalism, stalking, and para-sociality the dramatic overtone of SA and their brutal drawn out depiction makes it hard to consider these themes. My vitriol with this film is that, and I wish I could see these themes for what they do, but they are made opaque and inaccessible to me by this.

It's very hard to imagine the all male crew NOT looking like the long haired creep. I get that it's a critique of how sexualised female stars in the media become, but this has submerged so much into that it's become what it's been trying to warn against. It was sexual violence about women written by men for men.

I dont watch animes but every so often I watch an anime to make sure Im not making a mistake. Given the rapey bits and the cartoon nipples Im taking it this isn't for kids but it so often feels like it is. Dialogue is all blunt declamatory statements, no subtext. The characters are two dimensional placeholders that dont give any indication tht they exist in the world outside of the film. Any illusions this has of being hallucinatory or trippy are killed off by the film within a film that's there to spell out exactly what's happening to our main girl. Very silly and tedious stuff.

I felt like I was watching someone’s sick fantasy be recreated in an anime style and the cherry on top is that the director is a MALE. Very uncomfortable watch and just overall not enjoyable and it’s sick this is so highly rated but oh well. I’m also in an insanely bad mood and this made it worse

I cannot stress how much I hated this movie. The premise is interesting, the art is gorgeous, and yet I loathe this with every fiber of my being. I never want to watch this again, and to be honest, if this is a top ten movie for someone, I'm judging immensely. This being someone's favorite movie is an immediate way for me to decide that that person is no longer someone I will be listening to in terms of taste. I was looking forward to this one as I enjoyed Satoshi Kon's Paprika, and am aware of the huge influence this film had on Darren Aronofsky. While the shot transitions/ compositions and hallucinatory narrative structure are at times imaginative and compelling, the male gaze ick factor is distracting and dated. The principal character is heavily sexualised, and is put through a series of degrading humiliations that seem like a playing out of the creator's fantasies. There is an underlying mysogyny at play which i couldn't get past. Unfortunately, It made for uncomfortable viewing for me, negatively offsetting the films technical and visual qualities.

i probably don’t like this movie for really narcissistic reasons, it challenges my perception of myself as a relatively intelligent person, i felt like i was high throughout the movie cause i just couldn’t understand it, was it a dream? was the mc losing their mind? who was committing the murders? i couldn’t answer a single question . i watched and explainer video and it did answer some of these questions but it just wasn’t entertaining to watch, i wish i had the same experience as all my friends who seem to love this but it just didn’t resonate with me. i enjoyed the drama of the pop idol transitioning in careers, and the social commentary is top notch, the loss of innocence, the changes in perception, the ruination of a reputation, but i just didn’t care about anything else, i didn’t care about anyone who died. people compare this to black swan and honestly it’s not even close, atleast that movie is decipherable and had a genuinely powerful message to present to the watcher, this movie feels like it hates the viewer, confusing simply for the sake of confusion. i am the standard film larper, a24 fan arthouse nerd, but i think i understand the criticisms thrown at people like that now, just because a movie is hard to comprehend doesn’t mean its suddenly peak fiction, sometimes simple plots can convey more meaning and make you feel more emotion. EMOTION EMOTION. half way through writing this i understand the problem, i felt no emotion throughout the duration, it was a slog and hard work to get through.

While I think the movie has some very good scenes, the film is going for too much. It goes in between different plots and cant settle on one thing, the entire film fells like a mess of "HES CRAZY! NO SHES CRAZY!" over and over again until the climax of the film. I am not sure was it supposed to be a serial killer movie, a film about the stalking and extreme expectations of a popstar or about the mental deterioration of a popstar who is trying to change her career to acting while everything around her changes and shifts. While every one of these plots would have been good on their own, the movie blends them in awkwardly until the rushed climax .

I usually don’t watch anime films, in fact this is my second ever - behind Akira (which wasn’t very good imo).
